rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are astray from truth and caught in doubt and confused opinions; this includes unbelievers and religious innovators across sects.
rows.anchor: عن الحق، وسعر مما هم فيه من الشكوك والاضطراب في الآراء، وهذا يشمل كل من اتصف بذلك من كافر ومبتدع من سائر الفرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their former doubt and confusion brought the Fire upon them; as they were astray, they are dragged face-first without knowing where they go, and rebuked to taste Saqar.
rows.anchor: كما كانوا في سعر وشك وتردد أورثهم ذلك النار، وكما كانوا ضلالا سحبوا فيها على وجوههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates everything according to a measure and guides creatures to the measure assigned to them, as also stated in 25:2 and 87:1–3.
rows.anchor: أي: قدر قدرا، وهدى الخلائق إليه؛ ولهذا يستدل بهذه الآية الكريمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sunni imams use this and similar verses and sound hadiths to establish God's prior decree: He knew things before they existed and wrote them before creating them, against the Qadariyya, who arose late in the Companions' era.
rows.anchor: إثبات قدر الله السابق لخلقه، وهو علمه الأشياء قبل كونها وكتابته لها قبل برئها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed with the Prophet about decree, and these verses were then revealed; Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: جاء مشركو قريش إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يخاصمونه في القدر

rows.speaker: جد عمرو بن شعيب
rows.claim: The grandfather of ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb says these verses came down only concerning the people who deny decree; al-Bazzar transmits the report without stating a grade.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده قال: ما نزلت هذه الآيات

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report traced to the Prophet says the verses were revealed about people in the latter days of the community who deny God's decree; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه تلا هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When told people were discussing decree, Ibn Abbas said the verses concerned them, called them the worst of the community, forbade visiting their sick or praying over their dead, and threatened a denier.
rows.anchor: فوالله ما نزلت هذه الآية إلا فيهم: {ذوقوا مس سقر. إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر}

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said he would seize a man denying decree, then cited the Prophet: women of Banu Fihr would circle Khazraj as polytheists, the community's first shirk; their error would end in denying that God decrees good as well as evil.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "كأني بنساء بني فهر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar warned a Syrian friend in a letter not to write to him after hearing that he discussed decree, because the Prophet foretold people in the community who would deny it; Abu Dawud transmits it from Ahmad.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "سيكون في أمتي أقوام يكذبون بالقدر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: The Prophet called those who deny decree the community's Magians and said not to visit them when sick or attend their funerals; Ahmad transmits this route, which none of the six canonical compilers included.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لكل أمة مجوس، ومجوس أمتي الذين يقولون: لا قدر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: The Prophet foretold metamorphosis among the community's deniers of decree and heretics; al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmit it, and al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih gharib.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "سيكون في هذه الأمة مسخ

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: The Prophet said everything, including incapacity and cleverness, is by decree; Muslim alone transmits this report through Malik.
rows.anchor: عن طاوس اليماني قال: سمعت ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "كل شيء بقدرن حتى العجز والكيس

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound Prophetic hadith urges seeking God's help without helplessness, accepting events as God's decree and will, and avoiding if-only regrets because they open Satan's work.
rows.anchor: استعن بالله ولا تعجز، فإن أصابك أمر فقل: قدر الله وما شاء فعل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet told Ibn Abbas that all people together could not benefit or harm him beyond what God had decreed; the pens are dry and the scrolls folded.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الأمة لو اجتمعوا على أن ينفعوك بشيء، لم يكتبه الله لك

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: On his deathbed, ʿUbada instructed his son that true faith and knowledge require belief in good and bad decree: what missed him could not have hit him and what hit him could not have missed; the first creation was the pen, commanded to write all that would be until Resurrection. Al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih gharib.
rows.anchor: إن أول ما خلق الله القلم. ثم قال له: اكتب. فجرى في تلك الساعة بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: The Prophet said a servant must believe in four matters: God's oneness, Muhammad's true prophethood, death, resurrection, and decree, good and bad; al-Tirmidhi considers the route through Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi the sounder, and Ibn Majah also transmits it.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يؤمن عبد حتى يؤمن بأربع

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: God wrote the creatures' decrees 50,000 years before creating the heavens and earth; Ibn Wahb adds that God's Throne was then upon water. Muslim transmits it, and al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih gharib.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله كتب مقادير الخلائق قبل أن يخلق السموات والأرض بخمسين ألف سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All inhabitants of earth will die, as will the inhabitants of the heavens except whom God wills; only God's noble Face remains, because the Lord is ever-living and never dies.
rows.anchor: أن جميع أهل الأرض سيذهبون ويموتون أجمعون، وكذلك أهل السموات، إلا من شاء الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God first informed people about what He created, then informed them that all of it would pass away.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: أنبأ بما خلق، ثم أنبأ أن ذلك كله كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a transmitted supplication calling God the Ever-Living, Self-Subsisting, Creator of the heavens and earth, and the Possessor of Majesty and Honor, asking for mercy, rectitude, and protection from reliance on self or creation.
rows.anchor: يا حي، يا قيوم، يا بديع السموات والأرض، يا ذا الجلال والإكرام

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says one should not stop after reciting that all on earth perish, but continue through the declaration that God's Face remains.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: إذا قرأت {كل من عليها فان} ، فلا تسكت حتى تقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse parallels 28:88, that everything perishes except God's Face, and connects seeking God's Face with worship and charity in 18:28 and 76:9.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية كقوله تعالى: {كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه} [القصص:88]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's Face is characterized by Majesty and Honor: God is worthy to be revered without disobedience and obeyed without defiance.
rows.anchor: هو أهل أن يجل فلا يعصى، وأن يطاع فلا يخالف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Possessor of Majesty and Honor as Possessor of greatness and pride.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {ذو الجلال والإكرام} ذو العظمة والكبرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing all earth's people as alike in death and destined for the afterlife, God judges them justly and asks which of His favors they deny.
rows.anchor: ولما أخبر عن تساوي أهل الأرض كلهم في الوفاة، وأنهم سيصيرون إلى الدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two gardens are below the preceding pair in rank, virtue, and status, as the Qur'anic wording itself indicates.
rows.anchor: هاتان الجنتان دون اللتين قبلهما في المرتبة والفضيلة والمنزلة بنص القرآن

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A previously cited hadith describes two gardens with gold vessels and contents for those brought near, and two with silver vessels and contents for the people of the right.
rows.anchor: جنتان من ذهب آنيتهما وما فيهما، وجنتان من فضة آنيتهما وما فيهما

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Abu Musa assigns the two golden gardens to those brought near and the two silver gardens to the people of the right.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو موسى: جنتان من ذهب للمقربين، وجنتان من فضة لأصحاب اليمين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets below as lower in degrees.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: {ومن دونهما جنتان} من دونهما في الدرج

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets below as lower in merit.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: من دونهما في الفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first pair's preceding mention signals special concern and superiority; the following phrase that these gardens are below them confirms the earlier pair's higher rank.
rows.anchor: أنه نعت الأولين قبل هاتين، والتقديم يدل على الاعتناء ثم قال: {ومن دونهما جنتان}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier gardens have branching boughs or diverse pleasures, whereas these are dark green from abundant watering.
rows.anchor: وقال هناك: {ذواتا أفنان} : وهي الأغصان أو الفنون في الملاذ، وقال هاهنا: {مدهامتان} أي سوداوان من شدة الري

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the gardens have darkened from greenness because they received plentiful water; elsewhere he glosses the word simply as green.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في قوله: {مدهامتان} قد اسودتا من الخضرة، من شدة الري من الماء

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, glosses the gardens as green; similar glosses are transmitted from Abu Ayyub, Ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Abi Awfa, ʿIkrima, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid in one report, ʿAta, ʿAtiyya al-ʿAwfi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yahya ibn Rafiʿ, and Sufyan al-Thawri.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {مدهامتان} : قال: خضراوان

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says the gardens are filled with greenness.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: {مدهامتان} : ممتلئتان من الخضرة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they are green from abundant watering and luxuriant.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: خضراوان من الري ناعمتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The freshness follows from branches luxuriantly verdant and interwoven with one another.
rows.anchor: ولا شك في نضارة الأغصان على الأشجار المشبكة بعضها في بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first pair has two flowing springs, while the second has two gushing springs; flowing is stronger than gushing.
rows.anchor: أي فياضتان. والجري أقوى من النضخ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the springs as abundant and overflowing.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أي فياضتان

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the springs are full and do not run dry.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {نضاختان} أي ممتلئتان لا تنقطعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first gardens' paired fruit is broader and more varied; the indefinite fruit here does not cover every kind, so dates and pomegranates are specified after the general term and singled out for their excellence.
rows.anchor: الأولى أعم وأكثر في الأفراد والتنويع على فاكهة، وهي نكرة في سياق الإثبات لا تعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dates and pomegranates follow fruit as particular items after a general category, a construction al-Bukhari and others discuss; they are singled out because of their excellence over other fruits.
rows.anchor: ولهذا فسر قوله: {ونخل ورمان} من باب عطف الخاص على العام، كما قرره البخاري وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jaj water is bitter and brackish, unfit for drinking or cultivation; people should thank God for sending sweet, fresh rain, which supplies drink, grazing, crops, and fruit, as 16:10–11 says.
rows.anchor: أي: زعاقا مرا لا يصلح لشرب ولا زرع، {فلولا تشكرون} أي: فهلا تشكرون نعمة الله عليكم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report through Jabir and Abu Jaʿfar says that when the Prophet drank water he praised God for giving sweet, fresh water by mercy rather than making it salty and bitter because of sins; no grade is stated.
rows.anchor: عن جابر، عن أبي جعفر، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه إذا شرب الماء قال: "الحمد لله الذي سقانا عذبا فراتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire people kindle is struck from fire-sticks and drawn out of its source.
rows.anchor: أي: تقدحون من الزناد وتستخرجونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God placed fire in its source wood; Arabs used the two trees marakh and ʿafar, rubbing green twigs together until sparks fell between them.
rows.anchor: بل نحن الذين جعلناها مودعة في موضعها، وللعرب شجرتان: إحداهما: المرخ، والأخرى: العفار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada interpret the kindled fire as a reminder of the greater Fire, Hell.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، وقتادة: أي تذكر النار الكبرى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada transmits a mursal Prophetic report that earthly fire is one part out of seventy of Hellfire; when people say it suffices, the Prophet replies that it was struck with water twice so people can benefit from and approach it.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: ذكر لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يا قوم، ناركم هذه التي توقدون جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet said earthly fire is one of seventy parts of Hellfire and was struck by the sea twice; otherwise God would have made no one benefit from it. Ahmad transmits this route.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن ناركم هذه جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In a report from Abu Hurayra, the Prophet says human fire is one of seventy parts of Hellfire; when told it is sufficient, he says Hellfire exceeds it by sixty-nine parts. Bukhari and Muslim transmit the report; another Muslim wording says all sixty-nine are as hot as it.
rows.anchor: نار بني آدم التي يوقدون جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits from Abu Hurayra that Hellfire is seventy times darker than earthly fire; al-Diya al-Maqdisi notes Ibn Musʿab transmitted it from Malik without raising it to the Prophet and considers it to meet the conditions of sound hadith.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أتدرون ما مثل ناركم هذه من نار جهنم؟ لهي أشد سوادا من

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and al-Nadr ibn ʿArabi understand those who benefit as travelers; Ibn Jarir prefers this, deriving it from the expression that a house is left empty when its inhabitants depart.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والضحاك، والنضر بن عربي: معنى {للمقوين} المسافرين

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another view derives the word from al-qiy and al-qiwa, meaning a barren, empty, distant place far from settled areas.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: القي والقواء: القفر الخالي البعيد من العمران

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam interprets those who benefit as the hungry.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: المقوي هنا الجائع

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, in reports from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym and Sufyan from Jabir al-Juʿfi, says the benefit is for residents and travelers and for any food that needs fire.
rows.anchor: وقال ليث ابن أبي سليم، عن مجاهد: {ومتاعا للمقوين} للحاضر والمسافر، لكل طعام لا يصلحه إلا النار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In Ibn Abi Najih's report, Mujahid interprets those who benefit as all people who enjoy it; ʿIkrima is also reported to hold this view.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد قوله: {للمقوين} المستمتعين، الناس أجمعين. وكذا ذكر عن عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The all-people interpretation is broader: rich and poor, residents and nomads need fire for cooking, warmth, light, and other uses. God put it in stones and pure iron, so travelers could carry tools and kindle it as needed; travelers are named though the benefit is universal.
rows.anchor: وهذا التفسير أعم من غيره، فإن الحاضر والبادي من غني وفقير

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report through a man from the Muhajirun of Qarn says Muslims share three things: fire, pasture, and water; Ahmad and Abu Dawud transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن رجل من المهاجرين من قرن، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "المسلمون شركاء في ثلاثة: النار والكلأ والماء

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet said three things may not be withheld: water, pasture, and fire; Ibn Majah transmits it with a good chain.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ثلاث لا يمنعن: الماء والكلأ والنار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas adds that charging for these shared items is forbidden, but its chain contains the weak narrator ʿAbd Allah ibn Kharrash ibn Hawshab.
rows.anchor: وله من حديث ابن عباس مرفوعا مثل هذا وزيادة: "وثمنه حرام" (4) . ولكن في إسناده "عبد الله بن خراش بن حوشب" وهو ضعيف

words: كُبِتُوا۟ كَمَا كُبِتَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who oppose God and His Messenger and defy His law are humiliated, cursed, and shamed as similar people before them were.
rows.anchor: أي: أهينوا ولعنوا وأخزوا، كما فعل بمن أشبههم ممن قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's clear signs are opposed only by a disbelieving, immoral, arrogant person who obstinately resists.
rows.anchor: واضحات لا يخالفها ولا يعاندها إلا كافر فاجر مكابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humiliating punishment answers their arrogance in refusing to follow God's law, submit to it, and humble themselves before Him.
rows.anchor: في مقابلة ما استكبروا عن اتباع شرع الله، والانقياد له، والخضوع لديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Resurrection, God gathers the first and last people together on one plain and tells them what good and evil they did.
rows.anchor: وذلك يوم القيامة، يجمع الله الأولين والآخرين في صعيد واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has counted and preserved their deeds even though they have forgotten them; He witnesses everything, so nothing is absent, hidden, or forgotten from Him.
rows.anchor: أي: ضبطه الله وحفظه عليهم، وهم قد نسوا ما كانوا عليه

words: إلا هو معهم أين ما كانوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many report consensus that God's being with people means His knowledge is with them; Ibn Kathir affirms that meaning and adds that His hearing and sight encompass them everywhere, with nothing hidden.
rows.anchor: حكى غير واحد الإجماع على أن المراد بهذه الآية معية علم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows, hears, and sees private speech, while His messengers record it too; Ibn Kathir connects this to 9:78 and 43:80.
rows.anchor: ورسله أيضا مع ذلك تكتب ما يتناجون به، مع علم الله وسمعه لهم

rows.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: Ahmad observes that the passage opens with knowledge and closes with knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أحمد: افتتح الآية بالعلم، واختتمها بالعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor migrants deserving the spoils of war left their homes and opposed their people seeking God's favor and pleasure, and supported God and His Messenger; their deeds confirm their words, and they are the leading migrants.
rows.anchor: أي: خرجوا من ديارهم وخالفوا قومهم ابتغاء مرضاة الله ورضوانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Anṣar settled in the abode of migration before the migrants and believed before many of them.
rows.anchor: أي: سكنوا دار الهجرة من قبل المهاجرين وآمنوا قبل كثير منهم

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar urged the next caliph to recognize the first migrants' rights and honor, and to treat the Anṣar well, accepting their good deeds and forgiving their wrongdoers; al-Bukhari transmits it here too.
rows.anchor: قال عمر: وأوصي الخليفة [من] (1) بعدي بالمهاجرين الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Anṣar's generosity and noble character led them to love the migrants and support them from their wealth.
rows.anchor: أي: من كرمهم وشرف أنفسهم، يحبون المهاجرين

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that migrants praised the Anṣar for supporting them in scarcity and giving generously, sharing pleasant livelihood and expenses; they feared the Anṣar would take all the reward. The Prophet replied that they would not, as long as migrants praised them and prayed for them. Ibn Kathir had not seen this route in the books.
rows.anchor: قال المهاجرون: يا رسول الله، ما رأينا مثل قوم قدمنا عليهم أحسن مواساة في قليل

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that when the Prophet offered the Anṣar lands in Bahrain, they would accept only if migrants received the same; the Prophet told them to be patient until they met him because favoritism would follow his death. Bukhari alone transmits this route.
rows.anchor: دعا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الأنصار أن يقطع لهم البحرين، قالوا: لا إلا أن تقطع لإخواننا من المهاجرين مثلها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Anṣar offered to share their date palms with the migrants; the Prophet declined, so they offered to tend them and share the harvest, and the migrants accepted. Bukhari transmits this without Muslim.
rows.anchor: قالت الأنصار: اقسم بيننا وبين إخواننا النخيل. قال: لا. فقالوا: تكفونا المؤنة ونشرككم في الثمرة
